did_you_know.text: The verse presents the LORD as the owner of the earth, the world, and everyone who lives in it: not only the land, but also all the people living on it belong to him.
The psalmist describes the earth’s foundations using imagery of seas and rivers, emphasizing that the world stands by the LORD’s power.
The verse contains two parallel questions: Who may ascend the mountain of the LORD, and who may stand in his holy place?
The answer describes a person worthy of approaching the holy place in two ways: with clean hands, meaning integrity in actions, and a pure heart.
The verse also requires honesty in speech and commitments: the worthy person does not make false vows or swear deceitfully.
According to the psalm, blessing and righteousness come from the LORD; they are not presented as merely human achievements.
The verse calls those who seek the LORD’s face “his seekers” and mentions Jacob in this description.
The psalmist addresses the gates with commands, inviting them to rise and open for the arrival of the “King of glory.”
When asked who the King of glory is, the psalm answers: the LORD, strong and mighty, mighty in battle. At the end, it adds the title “the LORD of hosts.”
